page: Vultr voc-g-64c-192gb-960s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor. The hardware configuration includes 64 dedicated vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor features 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. System memory consists of 192.0 GB of RAM, yielding 3.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is provided via a 960 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieved a top-tier rating in stress-ng single-core CPU performance and PassMark memory score. Multi-core execution is rated as strong, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 100,556.13 and a PassMark CPU score of 79,514.14. Memory bandwidth is consistently strong, reaching 4,968.98 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 340.62 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. In software compilation and ray tracing, the system scored in the top 25%. However, single-threaded compression tasks and Geekbench multi-core scores fell into the average tier, indicating a relative tradeoff in single-threaded throughput.

With its high core density and dedicated CPU allocation, this server offers a balanced resource profile for multi-threaded workloads. The 1:3 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides sufficient memory density for parallel processing without the overhead of memory-optimized configurations. It is suited for database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and multi-threaded decompression. Additionally, the system demonstrates strong capabilities in small-to-medium LLM inference, achieving top-tier text generation speeds of 53.85 tokens/sec on 7B models, making it viable for CPU-based machine learning inference tasks.
